description: Object registry of the tactile pipeline (objects.py). Order = object id of the multi-object models. Coordinates: the STL file's own frame in mm (+x towards the head: tines / bowl / blade). Parts: names[k] covers x >= x_starts_mm[k] (decreasing starts); below the last start is the last name; |normal . z| < edge_nz is 'edge'.

fork_stl.units_note: imported in mm when the project started (file name; 120.3 x 16.3 x 5.0 mm, a dinner fork)
fork_stl.import_command: python stl_to_mjcf.py ForkMilimeter.stl --name fork_stl --units mm --threshold 0.01 --face 21.6 0 --site tips 31 0 --site palm 4.5 0 --site neck -2 0 --site handle -45 0 --site handle_end -76 0 --tine-root 7.0 --active
fork_stl.material_note: one solid body; nothing in the mesh suggests another material
fork_stl.shape: bent dinner fork, 1.5 mm sheet, 5 mm tall: the tines and the handle end curve towards +z
fork_stl.mirror_note: top-view outline vs its mirror image y -> -y (results_multi/objects/import_report.json); mirror augmentation allowed
fork_stl.face_note: face down (tines curve down onto the table) and face up are different surfaces for the sensor

fork2_stl.units_note: longest extent 0.1203 file units; only metres give a cutlery length in 120-250 mm (120.3 mm); scaled x1000 to results_multi/objects/source_mm/Fork_mm.stl and imported in mm
fork2_stl.import_command: python stl_to_mjcf.py results_multi/objects/source_mm/Fork_mm.stl --name fork2_stl --units mm --threshold 0.01 --face 21.6 0 --site tips 31 0 --site palm 4.5 0 --site neck -2 0 --site handle -45 0 --site handle_end -76 0 --tine-root 7.0
fork2_stl.material_note: one solid body of uniform 2 mm thickness; nothing in the mesh marks a separate handle or another material, so steel throughout (default)
fork2_stl.shape: flat 2 mm plate with fork_stl's exact top-view outline (4 tines from x = 7 mm); not bent
fork2_stl.mirror_note: top-view outline vs its mirror image y -> -y (results_multi/objects/import_report.json); mirror augmentation allowed
fork2_stl.face_note: a flat, mirror-symmetric plate: face up and face down give the same surface to the sensor

parts.note: along the STL x axis like fork_stl's: the narrow part from -15 mm to where the head widens (x = 1 mm) is the neck (spoon) / bolster (knife); the head (bowl / blade) starts at 1 mm, the handle below -15 mm
